about: Springbrook Hollow Farm Distillery takes its name from the spring that has supplied farms in this valley near Lake George for generations. Dave Bannon, who raised his family on the property and stabled horses in its barn, started the distillery with friends and neighbors in 2014, and the barn became their first still house and tasting room. The partners have since built a larger Adirondack-style distillery on Route 149, beside the original farm.

The barrel-strength bottling is the undiluted version of Springbrook’s Adirondack Blended Straight Bourbon: the distillery’s own straight bourbon married with straight bourbons sourced from other producers. Instead of being cut with spring water to the usual 43%, it is bottled at the strength it came from the barrel, 58% alcohol or 116 proof, after aging in new charred American oak. It appears in limited releases.

Springbrook’s notes point to heavy caramel and vanilla on the nose, oak and toffee on the palate, and a long finish that moves between dry and sweet. The whiskey earned a Silver medal, with 87 points, at the 2025 Bartender Spirits Awards, judged by working bartenders and bar managers, the same people who decide what goes behind a bar.
